newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees tight sunseed supply up to August.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees tight sunseed supply up to August.

text.p: World sunseed supplies and crushings will fall short of expectations in the second half of the 1996/97 world crop season, the Oil World newsletter said.
Citing global crop shortfalls and low stocks in the northern hemisphere, it said this should contribute to higher prices of sunseed and sun oil over the next few months.
Argentina's crop was now put at 5.15 million tonnes, down from 5.56 million last year, and this meant lower seed, oil and meal exports, the publication said.
South Africa's sunseed crop, which will be harvested in April/June, had suffered weather damage and should only be around 450,000 tonnes, down by 300,000 from last year.
Combined sunseed exports from Russia and the Ukraine were forecast to fall to 300,000 tonnes in March/August 1997 after 900,000 tonnes in the same period last year.
This was in sharp contrast to combined export shipments in September/February 1996/97 of 1.3 million tonnes, almost double the volume in the same 1995/96 period.
Exporting mostly to the European Union, the two had depleted their stocks, Oil World said.
EU sunseed imports and crushings were forecast to fall sharply in March/August.
